disney-the-renaissance-and-the-empire.subtitle: How Disney went from a takeover target to the world's biggest storyteller.
overview: In 1984 Disney was worth more broken up than whole. Its studio had gone cold, its parks were underpriced, and corporate raiders were circling.

Over the next 35 years two leaders rebuilt it. Michael Eisner revived animation and raised what the parks earned. Bob Iger bought the studios that made the stories people loved most: Pixar, Marvel and Lucasfilm.
This book follows that turnaround, and the one idea underneath it: own great stories, then let every part of the company make money from them.

story.h: A kingdom worth more in pieces
p: By the early 1980s, the company Walt Disney built had lost its nerve. Walt had died in 1966, and for years afterwards the studio made decisions by asking what he would have done. The films got safer and smaller. Most of the profit came from the theme parks and the land around them, not from new stories.

Wall Street noticed. In 1984 the investor Saul Steinberg bought a large stake and threatened a hostile takeover. His plan was simple: buy the company, sell off the parks, the film library and the real estate one by one, and walk away richer. Disney avoided that only by buying his shares back at a premium, a tactic known as greenmail. The company survived, but it was clear it could not go on as it was.

Roy E. Disney, Walt's nephew, and the company's largest shareholders brought in two outsiders. Michael Eisner came from Paramount, where he had backed hit after hit. Frank Wells came from Warner Bros. and knew how to run the business side. Eisner would chase ideas; Wells would make sure they paid.

Their first moves were not glamorous. Ticket prices at the parks had barely moved in years, so they raised them. Classic films that had sat in the vault were released on home video and sold millions of copies. That money bought time, and they spent it on animation.

In 1989 The Little Mermaid brought audiences back. Beauty and the Beast, Aladdin and The Lion King followed within five years. Each one did more than fill cinemas. It sold toys, filled new rides, became a stage show and kept selling on video for years.

story.quote: A hit film was never the end of the story at Disney. It was the opening act.

p: None of this was new. In 1957 Walt had drawn a simple chart with the films in the middle and lines running out to the parks, the music, the books, the comics and television. Every part fed the others. A film made people want to visit the park, the park sold the toys, and the toys kept children asking for the next film.

Eisner put that chart back to work. It also explains why Disney paid $19 billion for Capital Cities/ABC in 1996. Owning a television network, and especially ESPN, gave Disney a place to show its stories and a steady stream of cash that did not depend on the next hit.

Then the partnership broke. Frank Wells died in a helicopter crash in 1994, and Eisner never found another partner like him. His choice of Hollywood agent Michael Ovitz as president ended badly within about a year. Relations with Pixar, the studio that had made Toy Story for Disney, turned bitter. Animation began to slip again.

Roy E. Disney left the board and started a campaign to remove Eisner. At the 2004 shareholder meeting, 43 percent of the votes refused to back him, a remarkable rebuke for a sitting chief executive. A year later the board named Bob Iger, a quieter operator from the ABC side, as his successor.

Iger's first big decision surprised almost everyone. Rather than keep fighting Pixar, he bought it in 2006 for $7.4 billion and put its leaders in charge of Disney's own animation studio. He followed with Marvel in 2009 and Lucasfilm, the home of Star Wars, in 2012, for roughly $4 billion each.

The trick was what he did not do. Each studio kept its own people and its own way of working. Disney added what it was best at: marketing, distribution, parks and merchandise. The flywheel now had far more stories to spin. In 2019 Disney completed its $71.3 billion purchase of 21st Century Fox and launched Disney+, a service built almost entirely on the library it had spent decades assembling.

Disney's comeback is often told as the story of two famous bosses. Underneath it is a quieter lesson. A company that owns stories people love can earn from them again and again, in places that have nothing to do with a cinema. The danger is forgetting that, as Disney did in the 1980s, or losing the people who know how to make the next one.
Over the next 14 days, each article in this book takes one part of that story and goes deeper.

avengers-doomsday.title: Avengers: Doomsday
avengers-doomsday.description: Marvel's biggest team returns, with Robert Downey Jr. back in the universe he started, this time as Doctor Doom.
avengers-doomsday.subtitle: Marvel's comeback bet, and the actor who started it all.
overview: Avengers: Doomsday is Marvel Studios' next team-up film, set to open on December 18, 2026. It reunites directors Anthony and Joe Russo, who made Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame.
Its biggest headline is a casting twist: Robert Downey Jr., who launched Marvel's film universe as Iron Man in 2008, returns as the villain Victor von Doom.

story.h: Why this film matters to Disney
p: Disney bought Marvel in 2009 for about $4 billion. The bet paid off on a scale few deals ever do: Avengers: Endgame alone earned about $2.8 billion worldwide in 2019.

The years after Endgame were bumpier, with more films and series and fewer giant hits. Doomsday is Marvel's attempt to make a team-up feel like an event again, by bringing back the people who made the last ones work.

story.quote: The actor who built Marvel's universe comes back to threaten it.

story.h: The return of a familiar face
p: Downey's Iron Man was the start of everything: the first Marvel Studios film, and the character whose sacrifice closed the original saga. Casting him as Doctor Doom, one of comics' great villains, turns that history into the story's hook.
The film leads into Avengers: Secret Wars, which follows a year later and is planned to close this chapter of the Marvel story.

Marvel released the final trailer on November 23, 2026, less than four weeks before opening. It begins with a quiet scene: Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter, played by Chris Evans and Hayley Atwell, talking about telling their son who his father really is.

Then a flash of light, and the Fantastic Four, led by Pedro Pascal's Reed Richards, land in their front yard. Earlier teasers had already brought back Thor, the X-Men and Wakanda, setting up the biggest crossover Marvel has tried.

black-clover-yuno.title: Black Clover: Yuno's Final Form
black-clover-yuno.description: Asta's rival had every gift from the start. How Yuno kept getting stronger, and the form he reached in the final battle.
black-clover-yuno.subtitle: The rival who had everything, and the power he found last.
overview: Black Clover is a fantasy manga by Yūki Tabata. It ran from 2015 to 2026, first in Weekly Shōnen Jump and then in Jump GIGA, and has sold more than 25 million copies. It follows two orphans, Asta and Yuno, who both dream of becoming the Wizard King, the strongest mage in the Clover Kingdom.

Asta was born with no magic at all. Yuno was born with almost too much: a rare four-leaf grimoire, a wind spirit at his side, and a talent everyone could see. The manga finished in May 2026, and the anime came back for a second season that October.

p: Asta and Yuno were left at the same church in the village of Hage, on the same night. They grew up as brothers and rivals, and at fifteen each received a grimoire, the book that holds a mage's magic.
Yuno's was a four-leaf clover grimoire, said to hold good fortune, and it drew the wind spirit Sylph, whom Asta nicknamed Bell. Asta's was a battered five-leaf book that holds anti-magic.

story.quote: One boy had no magic. The other had more than anyone. In the end they fought with the same power.

p: Joining the elite Golden Dawn squad, Yuno learned to fuse with Bell in a form called Spirit Dive, turning himself into living wind.

Later he learned where he really came from: he was a lost prince of the Spade Kingdom, and his mother's star magic was his too. He could make small stars and fire spells from them, and mix them with his wind.
In the last battle, against Lucius Zogratis, Asta did something no one expected: he shared his anti-magic with Yuno, through his Demon-Dweller sword.

Yuno combined it with Bell's wind and his star magic. One side of his body is wrapped in anti-magic and a demonic wing grows from his back. For the first time, the boy with every gift fights with the one power only Asta had.
The first anime ran for 170 episodes from 2017 to 2021. Crunchyroll announced a second season in July 2025, and it premiered in Japan on October 3, 2026, again made by Studio Pierrot.

iphone-17-pro.title: iPhone 17 Pro
iphone-17-pro.description: Apple's 2025 Pro phone gave up titanium for aluminum, stretched the camera across the back, and was built to run cool.
iphone-17-pro.subtitle: Why Apple's most powerful phone went back to aluminum.
overview: Apple announced the iPhone 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max on September 9, 2025. They were the biggest redesign of the Pro line in years: a new aluminum body, a camera area that runs the full width of the back, and a new A19 Pro chip.
The changes weren't only about looks. Most of them come back to one problem every phone maker now faces: fitting more power into a thin glass slab without it getting too hot.

p: The two previous Pro models were made of titanium, sold as tough and premium. The 17 Pro went back to aluminum: a single unibody piece of aerospace-grade 7000-series aluminum alloy.

Aluminum moves heat away far better than titanium. Inside, Apple added a vapor chamber, a sealed pocket of deionized water laser-welded into the frame, which spreads heat away from the chip. Apple says the result is up to 40% better sustained performance than the year before.

story.quote: Thin, powerful, cool to the touch: getting all three is the hardest promise in phones.

story.h: A camera built like a plateau
p: The cameras now sit on a raised, forged bar that stretches across the whole top of the back. All three rear cameras are 48 megapixels, and the telephoto reaches about 8x zoom at optical quality.
Apple says the plateau also frees up space inside for a bigger battery. It was one of the clearest signs of Apple's direction: the Pro is now as much a camera as a phone.
